about: Movement (run) class per battle sheet: light | heavy | robe (+ none for non-humanoids). Owner decision 2026-11-26: 달리기(이동)를 경량·중량·로브 세 부류로. Battle movement stays RUNNING: for heavy/robe that means the fastest natural gait for that body, not a slow walk. Frames are drawn over a skeleton/mannequin (PC session); never deform drawn art. Gait class is separate from the hit weight in motion_chars.json hit.sheets (how a body TAKES a blow): e.g. warlord/khan/frostjarl are hit 'heavy' but gait light. Plan + Korean table: docs/plans/2026-11-26_gait_classes.md.
source: each sheet's idle cell (frame 0) plus attack/hit cells cropped from assets/art/sheets/*.png and viewed, plus the CHARACTER text in art/requests/phase3/<pkg>/README.md
owner_quote: 달리기(이동)에 대해 3가지 부류를 정하고 싶어. 경량, 중량, 로브. 펑퍼짐한 천 복장을 입고 뛰는것도 좀 부자연스러울거고, 중장비를 갖추면 당연히 뛰는건 물론이고 몸이 저렇게 땅에서 떨어지거나 몸을 앞으로 기울인 채로 가누기도 어려울테니까.

rules_of_thumb.heavy: plate armour / full metal or scale / tower shield / very large weapon carried
rules_of_thumb.robe: long robes, gowns, cassocks, long cloaks reaching below the knee that hide the knees and thighs
rules_of_thumb.light: everything else: leather, cloth to the knee, chain shirt with tabard/gambeson, cloaks or long OPEN coats over trousers where the legs read
rules_of_thumb.borderline: entries with a 'borderline' field carry the default in 'gait' and the reason the other class is defensible

light.summary: the accepted run: lean forward, press down in flight, rise a little after the landing is caught, hip nearly level, slight float, no hopping.
light.flight_phase: short (one cell R4/R8; feet only a few px off the floor)
light.arms: pump opposite to the legs (weapon hand carries the weapon)
light.stride_note: drawn stride 45.5 game px vs ~20 px per code step at 1x -> the planted foot slides ~6-8 px per contact cell (fixed 2026-11-26 by cadence B in js/battle.js runCells: stance cells consume ds/4 each, so the foot stays planted at 1x/2x; unit speed unchanged - owner chose B only)
light.who: leather, cloth to the knee, chain shirt with tabard/gambeson, cloaks or long OPEN coats over trousers where the legs read

heavy.summary: heavy armour / tower shield / very large weapon: cannot really run. Fastest natural gait for that body = a heavy, purposeful, FAST trudge (not a stroll): NO flight phase (one foot always on the ground), torso upright, short stride, the weight dropped onto each footfall, arms held close and high.
heavy.flight_phase: none - every cell has one foot planted; both feet down at contact (double support)
heavy.torso: upright: lean 5 deg (4-6) from the hip to the neck, the same in every cell (draft 4.8-5.6); head level
heavy.hip: the weight drops ONLY at down (contact -> down -7 px source), then comes back up slowly; the push is never above contact; bob 4-10 px source (draft 7)
heavy.knee_lift: low (the lifted sole 5-13 px source above the floor), knees stay bent (passing 49-51 deg)
heavy.arms: held close and high as if a shield is carried in front (far arm, forearm across the front at chest height) and a weapon at the side (near arm, hand at the belt): swing only a few degrees (hand fore-aft range 7-18 px source)
heavy.stride_game_px: 23.5 (range 20-24; the cells are played planted: stride/4 per cell)
heavy.game_ms: 101 ms a cell at 58 game px/s (stride/4 / speed; slower units / 1.5x boss sheets stretch it)
heavy.feel: heavy grounded footfalls at a quick cadence (149 steps a minute at 1x): the weight is in the drop at down, not in a slow walk
heavy.who: plate armour, full metal or scale armour, tower shield, very large weapon worn/carried (giant maul)

robe.summary: loose long cloth: running in it looks unnatural. Fastest natural gait = a hurried, purposeful glide (not a stroll): NO flight phase, NO big knee lift, a small forward lean, short quick steps; the hem swings and hides the knees, only the feet flick out at the hem.
robe.flight_phase: none - one foot always on the ground; both feet down at contact
robe.torso: small hurrying lean: 7 deg (5-8) from the hip to the neck (draft 6.8-7.6)
robe.hip: smooth, nearly level glide: bob 0-8 px source (draft 5)
robe.knee_lift: small - the knees stay inside the cloth (cloth_front) in every cell; the lifted sole 5-10 px source above the floor
robe.legs: drawn mostly as hem shape; the front foot shows at the hem, the back foot peeks behind
robe.hem: pushed out at once by the stepping leg, falls back one cell late (down keeps the contact hem shape); hem bottom 38-52 px source above the floor
robe.arms: close: hands near the waist / on the staff, elbows 72-76 deg, small swing (hand fore-aft range 33-36 px source)
robe.stride_game_px: 22.2 (range 22-28; the cells are played planted: stride/4 per cell)
robe.game_ms: 96 ms a cell at 58 game px/s (a slightly quicker cadence than heavy: 156 steps a minute at 1x)
robe.who: long robes, gowns, cassocks/robes and long cloaks reaching below the knee that hide the knees and thighs

none.summary: non-humanoids keep their own movement (quad/bug/hover; gaitType() in js/battle.js). Not part of the three classes.

class_defaults.about: Defaults for units WITHOUT their own sheet and for commissioning FUTURE sheets. The gait of a unit on screen must follow the sheet actually drawn (Art.sheetFor: art portrait -> monster -> captain -> hero -> class master -> adv -> base). Today every adv/master unit falls back to sheet/class/<base> and must use THAT sheet's gait (e.g. a paladin drawn with the warrior sheet runs light). Lookup when deciding a gait: sheets[<the sheet used>] > class_defaults.master[key] > adv[key] > base[cls]; sheet-less captains use captain_style; enemies use enemy_tpl.

base_why.warrior: sheet/class/warrior: chain shirt + tabard + round shield

adv_why.paladin: 성기사: plate is the archetype (outfit #c9ced6 steel) - heavy if its own sheet is drawn in plate
adv_why.battlepriest: 전투사제: melee priest in mail - light

master_why.inquisitor: 심판관: battle-priest line, mail - light (the captain inquisitorlord is robe because of HIS drawn robe)
master_why.arbalest: 노궁 대장: heavy crossbow but no armour - light (cf. siegemaster)

class_defaults.captain_style_why: only for a captain without a sheet; current registered captain sheets use their entry above (which wins)
class_defaults.enemy_tpl_why: imp = man-sized humanoids (goblin, bandit, lizardman, skeleton); brute = trolls/orcs/yeti/frost giant king, big heavy bodies (borderline for plain 오크 - a light run is possible); demon = 마족 전사 (light unless drawn armoured).
